title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 62 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 433–434 (Night 62, continuing directly from nights-61), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 62 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān, still on the chapter on good manners (adab), finishes the story of Muʿāwiya, al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays and Maysūn, in which al-Aḥnaf describes how he conducts himself with others and with his wife, and then begins a story of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb's treasurer Muʿayqib. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-sittūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second and the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixty-second night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْأَحْنَفَ بْنَ قَيْسٍ قَالَ لِمُعَٰوِيَةَ لَمَّا سَأَلَهُ وَأَدِمِ السِّوَاكَ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ اثْنَيْنِ وَسَبْعِينَ فَضِيلَةً وَغُسْلُ الْجُمُعَةِ كَفَّارَةٌ لِمَا بَيْنَ الْجُمْعَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-Aḥnafa ibna Qaysin qāla li-Muʿāwiyata lammā saʾalahu wa-adimi al-siwāka fa-inna fīhi ithnayni wa-sabʿīna faḍīlatan wa-ghuslu al-jumuʿati kaffāratun li-mā bayna al-jumʿatayni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate-one, that al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said to Muʿāwiya when he asked him: And keep-up the tooth-stick, for in it are two and seventy virtues, and the bath of the Friday is an atonement for what is between the two Fridays.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said to Muʿāwiya, when he questioned him: Keep to the toothstick, for it has seventy-two virtues; and the Friday bath atones for what lies between one Friday and the next.
sentences.n: The sentence is loosely joined: what Muʿāwiya asked is not given, and al-Aḥnaf's advice begins abruptly with وَأَدِمِ "and keep up" (the imperative of أَدَامَ). السِّوَاك is the tooth-stick (the miswāk) used for cleaning the teeth.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ مُعَٰوِيَةُ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ لِنَفْسِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu Muʿāwiyatu kayfa raʾyuka li-nafsika
sentences.l: He said to him, Muʿāwiya: How is your opinion for your self?
sentences.i: Muʿāwiya said to him: And how do you conduct yourself?

sentences.t: قَالَ أَطَأُ بِقَدَمِي عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَنْقُلُهَا عَلَى تَمَهُّلٍ وَأُ رَاعِيهَا بِعَيْنِي
sentences.tr: qāla aṭaʾu bi-qadamī ʿalā al-arḍi wa-anqulu-hā ʿalā tamahhulin wa-urāʿīhā bi-ʿaynī
sentences.l: He said: I tread with my foot upon the earth, and I move it upon deliberation, and I watch-over it with my eye.
sentences.i: He said: I set my foot down upon the ground, move it deliberately, and keep my eye on it.
sentences.n: وَأُ رَاعِيهَا is printed as two pieces, وا and راعيها; read it as the one word وَأُرَاعِيهَا "and I watch over it".

sentences.t: قَالَ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ عَلَى نَفَرٍ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ دُونَ الْأُمَرَأِ
sentences.tr: qāla kayfa raʾyuka idhā dakhalta ʿalā nafarin min qawmika dūna al-umarāʾi
sentences.l: He said: How is your opinion when you enter upon a band from your people, without the commanders?
sentences.i: He said: And when you go in among a company of your own people, with no amirs among them?
sentences.n: الْأُمَرَأِ is printed with an alif-seat hamza at the end; it is the plural الأُمَرَاء "the commanders, amirs", and is read so.

sentences.t: قَالَ أُطْرِقُ حَيَاءً وَأَبْدَأُ بِالسَّلَامِ وَأَدَعُ مَا لَايَعْنِينِي وَأُقِلُّ الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: qāla uṭriqu ḥayāʾan wa-abdaʾu bi-al-salāmi wa-adaʿu mā lā yaʿnīnī wa-uqillu al-kalāma
sentences.l: He said: I lower-the-gaze modesty-wise, and I begin with the greeting, and I leave what does-not-concern-me, and I make-little the speech.
sentences.i: He said: I lower my eyes modestly, I begin with the greeting, I leave alone whatever does not concern me, and I say little.
sentences.n: The edition prints a shadda on وَأُقِلُّ, and it is kept. لَايَعْنِينِي is printed as one word: لَا "not" + يَعْنِينِي "it concerns me".

sentences.t: قَالَ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ عَلَى نُظَرَائِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla kayfa raʾyuka idhā dakhalta ʿalā nuẓarāʾika
sentences.l: He said: How is your opinion when you enter upon your equals?
sentences.i: He said: And when you go in among your peers?

sentences.t: قَالَ أَسْتَمِعُ لَهُمْ إِذَا قَالُوا وَلَا أَجُولُ عَلَيْهِمْ إِذَا جَالُوا
sentences.tr: qāla astamiʿu lahum idhā qālū wa-lā ajūlu ʿalayhim idhā jālū
sentences.l: He said: I listen to them when they speak, and I do-not range over them when they range.
sentences.i: He said: I listen to them when they speak, and I do not push in among them when they range about the talk.
sentences.n: جَالَ is "to go to and fro, range about"; here it evidently means ranging through the conversation. The force of عَلَيْهِمْ is not certain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ عَلَى أُمَرَائِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla kayfa raʾyuka idhā dakhalta ʿalā umarāʾika
sentences.l: And he said: How is your opinion when you enter upon your commanders?
sentences.i: He said: And when you go in to your own amirs?

sentences.t: قَالَ أُسَلِّمُ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِشَارَةٍ وَأَنْتَظِرُ الْإِجَابَةَ فَإِنْ قَرَّبُونِي قَرُبْتُ وَإِنْ أَبْعَدُونِي بَعُدْتُ
sentences.tr: qāla usallimu min ghayri ishāratin wa-antaẓiru al-ijābata fa-in qarrabūnī qarubtu wa-in abʿadūnī baʿudtu
sentences.l: He said: I give-greeting without sign, and I await the answer; and if they bring-me-near, I draw near, and if they put-me-far, I am far.
sentences.i: He said: I give greeting without any gesture and wait for a reply; if they draw me near, I come near, and if they keep me at a distance, I keep my distance.

sentences.t: قَالَ كَيْفَ رَأْيُكَ مَعَ زَوْجَتِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla kayfa raʾyuka maʿa zawjatika
sentences.l: He said: How is your opinion with your wife?
sentences.i: He said: And how do you act with your wife?

sentences.t: قَالَ أَعْفِنِي مِنْ هَذَا يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: qāla aʿfinī min hādhā yā amīra al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: He said: Excuse me from this, O commander of the believers.
sentences.i: He said: Spare me this, Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ is printed as one word; it is the caliph's title, "commander of the believers".

sentences.t: قَالَ أَقْسَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُخْبِرَنِي
sentences.tr: qāla aqsamtu ʿalayka an tukhbiranī
sentences.l: He said: I have sworn upon you that you inform me.
sentences.i: He said: I charge you by oath to tell me.

sentences.t: قَالَ أُحْسِنُ الْخُلُقَ وَأُظْهِرُ الْعِشْرَةَ وَأُوَسِّعُ النَّفَقَةَ فَإِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ خُلِقَتْ مِنْ ضِلَعٍ أَعْوَجَ
sentences.tr: qāla uḥsinu al-khuluqa wa-uẓhiru al-ʿishrata wa-uwassiʿu al-nafaqata fa-inna al-marʾata khuliqat min ḍilaʿin aʿwaja
sentences.l: He said: I make-good the disposition, and I show the companionship, and I widen the expenditure; for the woman was created from a rib, crooked.
sentences.i: He said: I am gracious in manner, I show warmth in our life together, and I am generous with her keep; for woman was created from a crooked rib.
sentences.n: The last clause echoes the saying that woman was created from a rib, and so is crooked. أَعْوَجَ is a diptote, hence the fatḥa as genitive.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَمَارَأْيُكَ إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُجَامِعَهَا
sentences.tr: qāla fa-mā raʾyuka idhā aradta an tujāmiʿahā
sentences.l: He said: And what is your opinion when you want to come-together with her?
sentences.i: He said: And what is your way when you wish to lie with her?

sentences.t: قَالَ أَلُمُّهَا حَتَّى تَسْتَطِيبَ وَأَلْثِمُهَا حَتَّى تَطْرَبَ فَإِنْكَانَ الَّذِي تَعْلَمُ طَرَحْتُهَا عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا
sentences.tr: qāla alummuhā ḥattā tastaṭība wa-althimuhā ḥattā taṭraba fa-in kāna alladhī taʿlamu ṭaraḥtuhā ʿalā ẓahrihā
sentences.l: He said: I gather-her-close until she finds-it-good, and I kiss her until she is moved-to-delight; and if it be that which you know, I throw her upon her back.
sentences.i: He said: I draw her to me until she is at ease, and I kiss her until she is stirred with delight; and when what you know of comes, I lay her on her back.
sentences.n: المها is printed unpointed and is obscure. أَلُمُّهَا "I gather her to me" (لَمَّ) is chosen by sense; أَلْمِسُهَا "I touch her" may be what was meant. "That which you know" is a discreet way of saying the act itself.

sentences.t: وَإِنِ اسْتَقَرَّتِ النُّطْفَةُ فِي قَرَارِهَا قُلْتُ اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهَا مُبَارَكَةً وَلَا تَجْعَلْهَا شَقِيَّةً وَصَوِّرْهَا أَحْسَنَ تَصْوِيرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ini istaqarrati al-nuṭfatu fī qarārihā qultu allāhumma ijʿalhā mubārakatan wa-lā tajʿalhā shaqiyyatan wa-ṣawwirhā aḥsana taṣwīrin
sentences.l: And if the drop settles in its resting-place, I say: O God, make it blessed, and do not make it wretched, and shape it the best of shapings.
sentences.i: And if the seed settles in its resting place, I say: O God, make it blessed and not wretched, and form it in the fairest form.
sentences.n: The edition prints a shadda on وَصَوِّرْهَا, and it is kept. النُّطْفَة is literally "a drop", the usual word for the seed of conception.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقُومُ عَنْهَا إِلَى الْوُضُوءِ فَأُفِيضُ الْمَاءَ عَلَى يَدَيَّ ثُمَّ أَصُبُّهُ عَلَى جَسَدِي ثُمَّ أَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا أَعْطَانِي مِنَ النِّعَمِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqūmu ʿanhā ilā al-wuḍūʾi fa-ufīḍu al-māʾa ʿalā yadayya thumma aṣubbuhu ʿalā jasadī thumma aḥmadu allāha ʿalā mā aʿṭānī mina al-niʿami
sentences.l: Then I rise from her to the ablution, and I pour the water upon my two hands, then I pour it upon my body, then I praise God for what He has given me of the blessings.
sentences.i: Then I rise from her to make my ablution: I pour water over my hands, then over my body, and then I praise God for the blessings He has given me.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مُعَٰوِيَةُ أَحْسَنْتَ فِى الْجَوَابِ فَقُلْ عَنْ حَاجَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Muʿāwiyatu aḥsanta fī al-jawābi fa-qul ʿan ḥājatika
sentences.l: And Muʿāwiya said: You have done-well in the answer; so say, concerning your need.
sentences.i: Muʿāwiya said: You have answered well; now tell me what you need.
sentences.n: فِى is printed with a dotless final ى (فى); it is the preposition "in".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ حَاجَتِي أَنْ تَنْقِىَ اللَّهَ فِى الرَّعِيَّةِ وَتَعْدِلَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالسَّوِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḥājatī an tanqiya allāha fī al-raʿiyyati wa-taʿdila baynahum bi-al-sawiyyati
sentences.l: And he said: My need is that you fear-God regarding the flock, and be-just between them with the levelness.
sentences.i: He said: What I need is that you fear God in your care of your subjects, and deal justly among them, with equal measure for all.
sentences.n: تَنْقِىَ is printed with ن where تَتَّقِىَ "you fear (God)" is evidently meant; it is read so in the translation. الرَّعِيَّة is the flock, a ruler's subjects.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَهَضَ قَائِمًا مِنْ مَجْلِسِ مُعَٰوِبَةَ فَلَمَّا وَلَّى قَالَتْ مَيْسُونُ لَوْلَمْ يَكُنْ بِالْعِرَاقِ إِلَّا هَذَا لَكَفَاءَ
sentences.tr: thumma nahaḍa qāʾiman min majlisi Muʿāwiyata fa-lammā wallā qālat Maysūnu law lam yakun bi-al-ʿirāqi illā hādhā la-kafāʾa
sentences.l: Then he got up, standing, from the sitting-place of Muʿāwiya; and when he turned away, Maysūn said: If there were not in Iraq but this one, it would suffice.
sentences.i: Then he rose and left Muʿāwiya's presence; and as he turned to go, Maysūn said: If Iraq had no one but this man, it would be enough.
sentences.n: مُعَٰوِبَةَ is printed with ب for ي; it is Muʿāwiya. لَكَفَاءَ is printed as it stands; لَكَفَاهُ "it would have sufficed" is evidently meant, and the sense is as translated. Maysūn is Muʿāwiya's wife, who has been listening.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ قَالَتْ وَهَذِهِ النُّبْذَةُ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ بَابِ الْأَدَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nuzhata al-Zamāni qālat wa-hādhihi al-nubdhatu min jumlati bābi al-adabi
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: And this brief-extract is of the sum of the chapter of manners.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: This little passage belongs to the chapter on good manners.
sentences.n: النُّبْذَة is a short piece, an extract. الأَدَب is good manners, polite learning; it is the heading under which she has been quoting these sayings and stories.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مُعَيْقِبٌ عَامِلًا عَلَى بَيْتِ الْمَالِ فِي خِلَافَةِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu kāna Muʿayqibun ʿāmilan ʿalā bayti al-māli fī khilāfati ʿUmara ibni al-Khaṭṭābi
sentences.l: And know, O king, that Muʿayqib was a worker over the house of the wealth in the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
sentences.i: And know, O king, that Muʿayqib was the officer in charge of the public treasury in the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
sentences.n: Muʿayqib is the name reports give to ʿUmar's keeper of the treasury (بَيْت الْمَال, "the house of wealth"). The night breaks off before the anecdote is told.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَٰدَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahr Zād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night: morning overtakes Shahrazād and she stops the "permitted speech", the story she was allowed to tell. The print writes her name as two words and without the alif, شَهْرَ زَٰدَ; it is kept so.
